alex: Quick sync  need a lightweight 1-pager + SDR soundbites vs cloud AI platforms/infra vendors. Ship to sales by EOD Wed.
jamie: Scannable only  3 claims, 3 proofs, 3 rebuttals. SDRs hate long reads. :thumbsup:
priya: Focus: predictable unit economics, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, graceful degradation/fallbacks. Short proof points.
tom: Add 'when to escalate' flow for inbound leads (cost/latency/regulatory). Route compliance asks to AE before demo.
morgan: Field asks: discovery one-liners like: "How do you model tail-latency under peak load?" and "Who owns model rollbacks?" Good openers.
alex: Draft copy, feedback inline:
```
Claim 1: Predictable inference unit cost  fewer surprises at month-end.
Proof: Dedicated pools + intelligent batching + per-route cost insights.
Rebuttal: "Our cloud plan autoscale" -> Autoscale increases variable spend. We offer reserved capacity with burst controls and transparent per-token math.

Claim 2: Consistent behavior across Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
Proof: Single API + rollout controls + unified observability.
Rebuttal: "We self-host for isolation" -> We support on-prem and VPC with same control plane and eval tooling; no separate stacks to maintain.

Claim 3: Reliability-first serving with graceful fallbacks.
Proof: Policy routing + model variants + automatic fallback keeps apps online.
Rebuttal: "We just retry/queue" -> Retries add latency; routing and KV caching reduce tail latency without blind retry loops.
```
jamie: Add bench line: "Typical customer sees 20-40% lower per-token cost after batching + caching" labeled "typical".
priya: +1 to "typical" and add footnote: sample workloads 1-2k req/sec mix chat/generation.
tom: Suggested inbound routing rules for SDR ops:
- cost/ops/throughput mentions -> tag #sales-inbound cost-track
- SLA/compliance -> #ae-enterprise-queue
- Benchmarks/RFPs -> #field-research attach eval request
morgan: SDR soundbites: 
- Vendor lock: "Keep flexibility  same API across hosted/dedicated/private."
- Cost surprise: "Reserved capacity + per-route cost breakdown = predictable spend."
- Reliability: "Fallback policies mean degraded responses, not silence."
alex: Two asks before send: 1) simple visual showing routing/fallback flow; 2) final sign-off on bench sentence.
